prose: Quanta covers the standout result among the 377 OpenAI announced on October 6, 2026: a proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, a weaker form of the 160-year-old Riemann hypothesis about the distribution of prime numbers. Stanford's Jared Duker Lichtman calls it the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far by quite a margin, and describes the implications of even this limited form as staggering. The piece examines what happens now: how mathematicians go about verifying a machine proof of this scale, what the quasi-RH result unlocks in number theory, and whether the full Riemann hypothesis is meaningfully closer.
highlights: OpenAI's Oct 6 batch of 377 results included a proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
Quasi-RH is a weaker form of the 160-year-old Riemann hypothesis on prime distribution
Lichtman (Stanford): 'most significant AI-for-math achievement so far, by quite a margin'
Implications of even the limited result described as staggering
Open questions: verification of machine proofs at this scale, and how much closer full RH now is
